title: What a river cleanup can and cannot fix

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Volunteer group RiverWatch removed nearly two tonnes of rubbish from a local river last year. Coordinator Ben Harris, is that a success?

segments.speaker: Ben
segments.text: It is useful, but the number can be misleading if we treat cleanup as the whole solution. We can remove bottles and packaging from the riverbank, but if the same waste keeps entering upstream, volunteers are repeating the same work.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: What did you learn from recording the rubbish?

segments.speaker: Ben
segments.text: We sorted items by type and location. Takeaway containers were concentrated near two car parks, while small plastic fragments were spread much more widely. That information helped the council place bins differently and speak to nearby businesses.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Has the amount of waste fallen?

segments.speaker: Ben
segments.text: In the two car-park areas, yes. But we are cautious about claiming a river-wide improvement because rainfall changes how much waste moves and where it collects. One clean-looking weekend does not prove a long-term trend.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: So cleanup also becomes a way of collecting evidence.

segments.speaker: Ben
segments.text: Exactly. Removing waste matters, but understanding how it arrives is what can prevent the next bag from filling up.

questions.prompt: Why does Ben say the two-tonne figure can be misleading?
options: The group did not weigh the rubbish.
Cleanup alone does not stop new waste entering upstream.
The river has no upstream area.
questions.explanationJa: removeしてもupstreamから新たに入れば根本解決ではないためです。

questions.prompt: Give two patterns the volunteers found by sorting the rubbish.
markscheme: Takeaway containers were concentrated near two car parks.
Small plastic fragments were spread more widely.
questions.explanationJa: takeaway containerはcar park周辺、small fragmentは広く分布していました。

questions.prompt: How did the council use the data?
options: It changed bin placement and contacted nearby businesses.
questions.explanationJa: bin placementとbusinessへの働きかけに使いました。

questions.prompt: Choose TWO reasons Ben is cautious about claiming river-wide improvement.
options: A single clean weekend does not show a long-term trend.

questions.prompt: Ben says understanding how waste arrives can help ________ the next bag from filling up.
questions.explanationJa: source理解がfuture wasteのpreventにつながります。

questions.prompt: What broader role does cleanup play for RiverWatch?
options: Both removing waste and collecting evidence about its sources
questions.explanationJa: cleanupとevidence collectionの二つの役割があります。

title: The repair café on Saturday mornings

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: Every Saturday, volunteers at a repair café help residents fix small appliances, clothes and bicycles. Organizer Rosa Chen, is the main goal reducing waste?

segments.speaker: Rosa
segments.text: Waste reduction is important, but the learning matters too. If someone watches a volunteer replace a cable safely or sew a torn seam, they may try a simple repair themselves next time instead of immediately replacing the item.

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: Can every object be repaired?

segments.speaker: Rosa
segments.text: No. Sometimes spare parts cost more than the object, or a sealed design makes safe repair unrealistic. We tell people honestly when replacement is the better option. Repair culture should not become guilt about every item that fails.

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: How do you handle safety?

segments.speaker: Rosa
segments.text: Volunteers work only within their skills, and electrical items are tested before they leave. If we cannot confirm a repair is safe, we do not hand the item back as if the problem is solved.

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: What would make repair easier beyond the café?

segments.speaker: Rosa
segments.text: Access to spare parts and repair information. Community skill helps, but product design and manufacturer support still shape whether repair is practical.

questions.prompt: What goal does Rosa add to waste reduction?
questions.explanationJa: waste reductionに加えlearning/skill sharingを重視します。

questions.prompt: Give two reasons an item may not be practical to repair.
markscheme: Spare parts may cost more than the item.
A sealed design may make safe repair unrealistic.

questions.prompt: What does Rosa mean by avoiding 'guilt'?
options: People should repair dangerous objects themselves.
Not every failed item can or should be repaired.
questions.explanationJa: すべてのitemを必ずrepairすべきだとは考えていません。

questions.prompt: Choose TWO safety practices used at the café.
options: Electrical items are tested before leaving.
Every object is opened by beginners.
Unsafe repairs are returned without warning.
Testing is avoided to save time.
questions.explanationJa: skill範囲とelectrical testingが安全対策です。

questions.prompt: Rosa says manufacturer support helps determine whether repair is ________.
questions.explanationJa: manufacturer supportがrepairのpracticalityに影響します。

options: Community repair can help, but design and support also matter.
Every product can be repaired cheaply.
questions.explanationJa: community effortだけでなくdesignやmanufacturer supportも必要という立場です。

segments.speaker: Moderator
segments.text: A school plans to turn part of its closely cut lawn into a wilder habitat. Biology teacher Mr Evans, what is the aim?

segments.speaker: Evans
segments.text: More variety. A short lawn offers limited shelter and food. Longer grass, native flowers and a small log area can support insects and other species while giving students a place to observe ecology directly.

segments.speaker: Moderator
segments.text: Grounds manager Kelly Brown, do you have concerns?

segments.speaker: Kelly
segments.text: Maintenance changes rather than disappears. A wild area still needs paths, checks for invasive plants and decisions about when to cut. If people think 'rewilding' means simply doing nothing, the site can become difficult to use and manage.

segments.speaker: Moderator
segments.text: Student Maya Patel, what do students want?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: We want access without damaging the habitat. Raised paths would help, and signs could explain why some areas look untidy compared with the old lawn. If people understand the purpose, they may be less likely to treat the space as neglected.

segments.speaker: Evans
segments.text: We also need to collect baseline data before making big claims. Counting pollinators after one summer is useful, but weather varies. The project should be monitored over several years.

segments.speaker: Kelly
segments.text: And accessibility must remain part of the design. A habitat project that creates barriers for wheelchair users would solve one problem by creating another.

segments.speaker: Moderator
segments.text: So the proposal combines biodiversity, education, maintenance and inclusive access rather than treating rewilding as a single-purpose project.

questions.prompt: What is Evans's main ecological aim?
options: Increase habitat variety for insects and other species
Keep every area as short lawn
questions.explanationJa: habitat varietyを増やしinsectsなどを支えることが目的です。

questions.prompt: Give two maintenance tasks Kelly says will still be needed.
markscheme: Maintain paths and/or check for invasive plants.
Decide when areas should be cut / manage cutting schedules.
questions.explanationJa: paths、invasive plants、cutting timingなどのmaintenanceが残ります。

options: To explain why wilder areas may look untidy and prevent them being seen as neglected
To ban students from the grounds
questions.explanationJa: untidyに見える理由を説明しneglectedと誤解されないためです。

questions.prompt: Choose TWO design or evaluation principles mentioned.
options: Use raised paths to reduce damage while allowing access.
Collect baseline data and monitor over several years.
questions.explanationJa: raised pathsとlong-term monitoringが重要です。

questions.prompt: Matching task: Match each speaker to the issue they emphasize: Kelly and Evans.
markscheme: Kelly — practical maintenance and inclusive / accessible design.
Evans — biodiversity benefits and careful long-term ecological monitoring.

questions.prompt: What is the moderator's final purpose?
options: To describe rewilding as a single-purpose gardening task
To summarize the different goals that must be balanced
